Not necessarily.

data.text:
90 minutes billed. 30 minutes beyond free time. Where did the other 60 come from?

ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE — NOT A CUSTOMER RESULT.

Imagine a gate log showing 08:30 arrival and 11:00 departure: 150 minutes on site.

If the applicable signed agreement allows 120 free minutes from arrival, with no exceptions, that leaves 30 minutes beyond the free period. An invoice billing 90 detention minutes raises a 60-minute question.

Not a proven error. Not a refund.

First verify appointment terms, the actual detention trigger, rate-effective dates, minimums, corrected invoices and credits.

One shipment. Two different rate sheets.

Which charge is actually correct?

Finding an old and a new rate table isn't enough to establish a billing error. The governing agreement—and the dates and amendments it makes relevant—determine which rate applies.

Our rate-version checklist:
01 / Identify the controlling contract and any incorporated tariff
02 / Check the date that determines which terms apply
03 / Reconcile amendments, exceptions, rebills and credits

A rate mismatch is a question to investigate, not an automatic refund.

Save this four-slide explainer for the next time a carrier invoice doesn't match the rate sheet on your desk.
